{{ElectionsMN}}
The '''2026 Minnesota gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Minnesota|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota|lieutenant governor]] of [[Minnesota]]. [[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party|Democratic]] senator [[Amy Klobuchar]] and [[Republican Party of Minnesota|Republican]] state House speaker [[Lisa Demuth]] are the nominees for their respective parties.

Democratic incumbent [[Tim Walz]] ran for a third term, but withdrew in January following a [[2020s Minnesota fraud scandals|scandal over fraud in state funded-social services]]. Following Walz's withdrawal, Klobuchar entered the Democratic primary and won the nomination with 89.7% of the vote against minimal opposition. In the Republican primary, Demuth defeated businessman [[Mike Lindell]], who was endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], and healthcare technology executive Kendall Qualls, who was endorsed by the state party, with 43.4% of the vote.

The winner of this election will be the first female governor of Minnesota.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Akaolisa |first=Tom |date=2026-08-17 |title=MINNEAPOLIMEDIA EDITORIAL {{!}} Minnesota Will Elect Its First Woman Governor. The Harder Task Is Governing a Fractured State {{!}} MinneapoliMedia |url=https://minneapolimedia.town.news/g/coon-rapids-mn/n/384781/minneapolimedia-editorial-minnesota-will-elect-its-first-woman-governor |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=minneapolimedia.town.news |language=en}}</ref> Republicans have not won a gubernatorial election in Minnesota since [[2006 Minnesota gubernatorial election|2006]].

== Democratic–Farmer–Labor primary ==
After Walz announced his withdrawal from the race, [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Amy Klobuchar]] launched a campaign for the governor's office on January 29, 2026.<ref>{{cite news| last1=Griffith| first1= Michelle| title= Sen. Klobuchar launches campaign for Minnesota governor| url= https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/01/29/sen-klobuchar-launches-campaign-for-minnesota-governor/| access-date= June 4, 2026| work= [[Minnesota Reformer]]| date= January 29, 2026}}</ref> Six other [[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party|Democratic-Farmer-Labor]] (DFL) candidates filed, none of whom have previously held elected office. Community organizer Kobey Layne challenged Klobuchar for the DFL's endorsement on May 30, 2026, but Klobuchar was endorsed on the first ballot alongside her running mate, [[Ben Schierer]].<ref name= "LayneMN">{{cite news| last1=Griffith| first1=Michelle| title=Klobuchar fights off challenge from left, wins DFL convention nod in bid for governor| url= https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/05/30/klobuchar-fights-off-challenge-from-left-wins-dfl-convention-nod-in-bid-for-governor/ |access-date= June 3, 2026| work= Minnesota Reformer| date= May 30, 2026}}</ref>

=== Caucus vote ===
On February 3, 2026, Minnesota DFLers held their party caucus.<ref>{{Cite web|last=TRIBUNE|first=MARIE TOLONEN MESABI|date=February 5, 2026|title=Amy Klobuchar tops DFL caucus straw poll| url= https://www.mesabitribune.com/news/local/amy-klobuchar-tops-dfl-caucus-straw-poll/article_d48347d8-e2e9-4943-8cff-c20837cd28d1.html|access-date=February 13, 2026|website=Mesabi Tribune|language=en}}</ref> Klobuchar won the party's straw poll for governor with approximately 72% of the vote.<ref name="ss"/>

On February 3, 2026, Minnesota Republicans held their party caucus.<ref>{{Cite news| last=Faircloth |first=Ryan |date= February 4, 2026| title= House Speaker Lisa Demuth poised to win GOP straw poll for governor, Qualls and Lindell trail behind| url= https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-gop-could-pick-a-frontrunner-for-governor-at-tuesday-precinct-caucuses/601575453|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260205131057/https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-gop-could-pick-a-frontrunner-for-governor-at-tuesday-precinct-caucuses/601575453|archive-date=February 5, 2026|access-date=February 10, 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Lisa Demuth won the party's straw poll for governor with approximately 32% of the vote.<ref name="ss">{{Cite web|title=Office of the State Of Minnesota Secretary of State|url=https://sos.mn.gov/elections-voting/how-elections-work/precinct-caucuses/|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260204173948/https://sos.mn.gov/elections-voting/how-elections-work/precinct-caucuses/|archive-date=February 4, 2026|access-date=February 10, 2026|website=sos.mn.gov|language=en}}</ref>
